cf.title: Preserve statistics targets with ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN TYPE

input.subject: Preserve statistics targets with ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN TYPE

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the problem is stated, and the fix restores settings the user chose. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is fixable. The entry is tagged Bugfix, both patches add fields to parse nodes, and the thread names no target branch. A committer has to decide the branch scope and which thread carries 0002.

brief.title: Keep statistics targets when alter column type rebuilds indexes and extended statistics
brief.problem: alter table ... alter column ... type (or set expression) recreates dependent indexes and extended statistics from their definition strings. Statistics targets set with alter index ... set statistics or alter statistics ... set statistics are not in those strings, so they silently revert to the default. This affects users who tune these targets.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 captures stxstattarget next to the owner in RememberStatisticsForRebuilding(), passes it through a new CreateStatsStmt field, and has CreateStatistics() store it. Patch 0002 captures per-column index targets where the index comment is captured, carries them in a new IndexStmt field, and has DefineIndex() apply them, including on partition indexes it creates.
user_visible_surface: Behavior change: extended statistics keep their stxstattarget after alter column type or set expression.
Behavior change: index expression columns keep their statistics targets after the rebuild, including indexes of exclusion constraints and indexes created on partitions.
C API: CreateStatsStmt gains a stxstattarget field, with -1 meaning the default (null) target.
C API: IndexStmt gains a field carrying per-column statistics targets.
author_claims: The bug is the same class of problem as the statistics owner reset fixed by commit 6713a6e04cb, and 0001 follows that fix's pattern.
Targets set directly on a partition's index are still lost when the rebuild recurses from the parent, matching existing behavior for comments.
The patches are tagged as a bug fix.
brief.thread_state: Melanie Plageman included a modified 0002 in another patch series; solai v tested v2 and reported both targets preserved. The author keeps both patches here because the other thread is still under discussion.
unclear: Melanie says she took 0002, but the author says the other thread includes 0001, so the material does not say which patch overlaps.
solai v's first review tested idx_scan counters, which these patches do not claim to change, so that test does not cover the fix.
The material does not say whether the fix is meant for back-branches, given the bug fix tag.
The material does not say why gram.y and parse_utilcmd.c change for 0001, or whether new syntax appears.
No committer has commented on the approach.

objections.title: Bug fix tag implies a backpatch, but parse node structs change
objections.failure_scenario: A committer backpatches both patches as a bug fix. An extension built against the earlier minor release creates an IndexStmt or CreateStatsStmt with makeNode() at the old size and passes it to DefineIndex() or CreateStatistics(). The server reads the new field past the end of the allocation, and the user sees wrong targets or a crash after a minor upgrade.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, and the brief notes that the material does not say whether back-branches are meant. Both patches add fields to parse nodes in parsenodes.h, which back branches avoid changing. The proposal does not say whether the fix is master-only or how a back-branch version would avoid the struct change.
objections.author_must_show: Is this fix meant only for master, and if not, how would a back-branch version keep IndexStmt and CreateStatsStmt unchanged?

critic.reasoning: The entry is tagged Bugfix, both patches add fields to parse nodes, and the thread does not name a target branch. Extensions do build IndexStmt nodes and call DefineIndex(), so the back-branch scenario is concrete, and fixable is the right severity.

refuted.title: Bug fix tag conflicts with new fields in IndexStmt and CreateStatsStmt
refuted.failure_scenario: If the fix is backpatched as tagged, an extension built against the older minor release creates an IndexStmt with makeNode and passes it to DefineIndex(). The extension allocates the old struct size, so the server reads the new statistics-target field past the end of the allocation. The user sees wrong targets or a crash after a minor upgrade.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry tags both patches Bugfix, and both commit messages add a field to a parse node in parsenodes.h. makeNode uses the struct size from the extension's compile-time headers, so even a field added at the end is not safe for callers that build these nodes themselves. The material does not say whether the fix targets back-branches or master only. If back-branches are meant, they need a different way to carry the targets.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this fix meant for back-branches, and if so, how would it carry the targets without changing the IndexStmt and CreateStatsStmt layout?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. It raises the same back-branch ABI question with the same scenario.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: IndexStmt and CreateStatsStmt each gain a field in parsenodes.h, and extensions build these nodes.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 touches gram.y, and the commit message does not say whether new syntax appears.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Kept statistics targets change what analyze collects after the rebuild, so plans can differ from today's post-rebuild plans.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix, but both patches change parse node structs that back branches normally keep stable.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The rebuild path in ATPostAlterTypeParse() gains two more properties to capture and reapply.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is this fix meant only for master, and if not, how would a back-branch version keep IndexStmt and CreateStatsStmt unchanged?
Why does 0001 change gram.y and parse_utilcmd.c, and does create statistics gain any new user-visible syntax?
Which of the two patches does the other series now carry, and should this entry keep only the patch that the other series does not include?
Does a target set directly on a partition's index still revert without notice when the rebuild recurses from the parent, and is that acceptable for a fix of silent loss?

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows the alter table rebuild path in tablecmds.c and the extended statistics code. Melanie Plageman took a modified 0002 into another series, but nobody in the thread has reviewed the approach of 0001.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the two new parse node fields and for the rebuild path keeping targets correct, including on partition indexes. If backpatched, the owner also signs for ABI stability in minor releases.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted a v2, rebased after the CFbot report and moved the entry to the next CommitFest.

priority.reason: Only users who set statistics targets on expression indexes or extended statistics are affected, but the loss is silent. Both patches are about 12 KB each, stay in the rebuild path, and follow the pattern already used for the comment and the owner.

provisional_note: Without the code, the gram.y change in 0001 and the way DefineIndex() applies targets to partition indexes could not be checked. The only review in the thread tested idx_scan counters, which the patches do not claim to change.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ALTER INDEX .. ALTER [COLUMN] col_num {SET,RESET}
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add `alter index ... alter [column] col_num set/reset (...)` so opclass parameters on an index column can be changed after `create index`, using a column number as `set statistics` does. The patch stores the new values in pg_attribute attoptions, checks them with index_opclass_options(), and does not rebuild the index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Changing an opclass parameter such as siglen without a rebuild leaves the index inconsistent with its options. Nathan Bossart reproduced test failures in hstore after `alter index hidx alter column 1 set (siglen=100)`, which went away after a REINDEX. Alexander Korotkov said the known uses for opclass options all need a rebuild and suggested keeping the options immutable until real cases for mutable ones appear. The author agreed the patch was not enough, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: All these cases require index rebuild to change the opclass option.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for ALTER COLUMN SET STATISTICS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops psql tab completion from adding "TO" after "ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET STATISTICS", where TO is not legal syntax. The patch completes nothing in that position.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch and marked it rejected after the tab-complete.c refactoring was committed, because that refactoring made the fix unnecessary. Earlier, Robert Haas suggested narrowing the generic rule that adds TO after any SET <word>, and the author did not want to rework that code while the refactoring was pending.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The now-committed tab-complete.c refactoring renders this unnecessary,
so I've marked this patch as rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Split index and table statistics into different types of stats
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits the cumulative statistics kind PGSTAT_KIND_RELATION into PGSTAT_KIND_TABLE and a new PGSTAT_KIND_INDEX, with index-specific counting macros and SQL-callable functions. The goal is sensible field names for index stats and lower memory use, since index entries currently carry unused table counters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stalled. Review comments from Andres Freund and Melanie Plageman were still open, and the author put the work on hold until the related "Generate pg_stat_get_xact*() functions with Macros" patch was done. After that patch was committed, no new version came; the CFM returned the entry because it no longer applied and tests failed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch no longer applies (with tests failing when it did), and the thread
has stalled.

precedents_retrieved.title: Inconsistency in owner assignment between INDEX and STATISTICS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal makes CREATE STATISTICS record the table owner as the owner of the statistics object, as CREATE INDEX does, in place of the user who runs the command. The patch sets stxowner from the relation's relowner in CreateStatistics() and keeps the permission check on the current user.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Khandekar pointed out that the documentation states statistics ownership is independent of the underlying table, so the creator owning the object is intended. He also showed that the reproduction was wrong: the statistics object was created in the default schema, and dropping it there gives the expected "must be owner" error. The author agreed with both points and withdrew the proposal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think, since there is no permanent association of ownership between
the table and the statistics, it makes sense for the user who is
running the create command to own the statistics, regardless of who
the user is, provided that the user has privileges.

precedents_retrieved.title: preserve timestamps when installing headers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `-p` to the `cp` calls in `src/include/Makefile` so installed headers keep their modification times. Together with `INSTALL="install -p"` passed to configure, this would stop `make install` from forcing a rebuild of extensions that depend on the headers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane pointed out that POSIX `cp -p` also preserves file ownership, which breaks the usual case of building as a normal user and installing as root. He and Peter Eisentraut also doubted the benefit was worth a change to the build rules, since ccache covers rebuild cost and build systems rarely track timestamps outside the tree. Discussion moved to switching header installation back to `$(INSTALL)` with user-supplied switches, but no revised patch appears in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It also specifies preserving file ownership,
which seems absolutely catastrophic for the standard use-case of
"build as some ordinary user, then install as root".

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Preserve versions of initdb-created collations in pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_upgrade preserve the recorded versions of collations created by initdb. In binary-upgrade mode, pg_dump would delete all initdb-created collations in the new cluster and dump CREATE COLLATION commands with version information, instead of updating the existing objects in place.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review showed that the patch makes the pg_upgrade check fail for clusters initialized with SQL_ASCII encoding, where ICU collations for that encoding do not exist, and that it leaves the recreated collations looking like user-defined objects. The author then questioned the approach and suggested not creating collations in initdb at all. The reviewer replied that the problem would go away if the separate per-object collation version patch set were committed, since that drops the collversion column. The author then marked the patch Returned with Feedback without further changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this problem goes away if we commit the per-object collation
version patch set[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Extended statistics in EXPLAIN
precedents_retrieved.summary: Show in EXPLAIN (VERBOSE) which extended statistics objects the planner applied to a scan node and to which clauses, so users can see whether a statistics object affects an estimate. The PoC patch stores this information in lists added to the Plan and deparses the clauses the way index quals are deparsed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The commitfest manager returned the entry because it had too little reviewer interest, and said the return was not a rejection. Earlier, Tom Lane objected that the feature exposes unstable planner internals, adds data and copying cost to every finished plan, and fails if a statistics object is dropped between planning and EXPLAIN. Robert Haas disputed this, and Tatsuro Yamada posted a rebase in January 2022, but no review followed before the entry was closed in August 2022.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Rather than code changes, what this patch needs is more community interest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Statistics for array types
precedents_retrieved.summary: When no array element passes the frequency threshold, ANALYZE would still keep the single most common element in the MCE statistics for an array column. The planner would then treat any other element as no more common than that one, so it no longer falls back to a fixed 0.5% selectivity.
precedents_retrieved.objection: It died of inactivity. Alexander Korotkov posted an alternative patch that stores cutoff_freq / nonnull_cnt as the minimum frequency, but neither the author nor Tomas Vondra replied to Alvaro Herrera's request for status. The CF manager set it to waiting for author and later returned it with feedback because there was no updated patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: There has been no activity on this thread in quite a while and no updated patch during this CF.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert non-text output formats for pg_dumpall
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert non-text output formats for pg_dumpall
Reverted commit(s): Add non-text output formats to pg_dumpall; Clean up nodes that  are no longer of use in 007_pgdumpall.pl; Fix casting away const-ness in pg_restore.c; Improve writing map.dat preamble; pg_restore: add --no-globals option to skip globals
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts the non-text (custom/directory/tar) output format support
for pg_dumpall added by 763aaa06f03 and its feature-specific follow-ups,
in line with Noah Misch's post-commit review which recommends reverting
and finishing the work through the commitfest.

Scope is deliberately minimal: only the feature itself is removed.
Independent improvements that merely touched the same files, or that were
committed alongside the feature but do not depend on its design, are
preserved.

Reverted (the feature):

  763aaa06f03  Add non-text output formats to pg_dumpall
  d6d9b96b404  Clean up nodes that are no longer of use in 007_pgdumpall.pl
  01c729e0c7a  Fix casting away const-ness in pg_restore.c
  c7572cd48d3  Improve writing map.dat preamble
  3c19983cc08  pg_restore: add --no-globals option to skip globals
  abff4492d02  Fix options listing of pg_restore --no-globals
  bb53b8d359d  Fix small memory leak in get_dbname_oid_list_from_mfile()
  a793677e57b  pg_restore: Remove dead code in restore_all_databases()
  a198c26dede  pg_dumpall: simplify coding of dropDBs()
  ec80215c033  pg_restore: Remove unnecessary strlen() calls in options parsing

Preserved (independent of the feature):

  b2898baaf7e  the check_mut_excl_opts() helper in src/fe_utils/option_utils.c
               and its use in pg_dump
  7c8280eeb58  pg_dump's conflicting-option refactor (and tests 002/005)
  be0d0b457cb  pg_dumpall's rejection of --clean together with --data-only
               (re-expressed directly, since pg_dumpall.c is otherwise
               returned to its pre-feature state)
  74b4438a70b  the dangling-grantor-OID GRANT fix (back-patched through 16)
  273d26b75e7, d4cb9c37765  independent pg_restore.sgml clarifications

Because the feature restructured pg_dumpall.c and pg_restore.c (pg_restore's
main() was split into restore_one_database() plus a dispatcher) and
interleaved its option checks with the conflicting-option refactor in the
same regions, the cosmetic check_mut_excl_opts() reflow of those two files'
option blocks is inseparable from the feature and comes out with it; the
behavior is unchanged.  The reusable helper and pg_dump's use of it are
unaffected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
Reverted commit(s): Use TRUNCATE to preserve relfilenode for pg_largeobject + index.; Fix failure to remove non-first segments of temporary tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Replace the stopgap fix I made in 0e758ae89 with a cleaner one.

The real problem with 4ab5dae94 is that it contorted this function's
logic substantially, by introducing a third code path that required
different behavior in the function's main loop.  That seems quite
unnecessary on closer inspection: the new IsBinaryUpgrade case can
just share the behavior of the other immediate-unlink cases.  Hence,
revert 4ab5dae94 and most of 0e758ae89 (keeping the latter's
save/restore errno fix), and add IsBinaryUpgrade to the set of
conditions tested to choose immediate unlink.

Also fix some additional places with sloppy handling of errno,
to ensure we have an invariant that we always continue processing
after any non-ENOENT failure of do_truncate.  I doubt that that's
fixing any bug of field importance, so I don't feel it necessary to
back-patch; but we might as well get it right while we're here.

Also improve the comments, which had drifted a bit from what the
code actually does, and neglected to mention some important
considerations.

Back-patch to v15, not because this is fixing any bug but because
it doesn't seem like a good idea for v15's mdunlinkfork logic to be
significantly different from both v14 and v16.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no row about the same or a similar idea. The thread points only to commit 6713a6e04cb (message #1), a committed fix for the statistics owner that this proposal extends, and to a parallel series that includes a modified 0002 (message #2). Neither reports an earlier rejection.
The behavior change only restores settings the user chose, pg_dump already emits these targets, and no new syntax is claimed. The gram.y change in 0001 could not be checked without the code.

Besides the back-branch ABI point, the patches only rewrite existing catalog values (stxstattarget, index attstattarget) inside the same transaction. They add no WAL records, no catalog columns, no on-disk format change and no protocol change.

No security or privilege objection. The patches restore statistics targets that an object owner already set, during an alter table that already requires table ownership, so no user gains a new power. Targets are still bounded by the existing maximum, and propagation to partition indexes matches the recursion alter index ... set statistics already does. The gram.y change in 0001 should be checked for new user-facing syntax, but even that would only let an owner set a value they can already set.

From the maintenance angle this is a narrow bug fix that follows existing patterns. IndexStmt already carries the index comment for the rebuild, and 0001 copies the owner fix in 6713a6e04cb. No hot-path cost, new dependency or new user surface appears in the material. The duplicate 0002 in Melanie's other series affects which thread gets committed, not whether the change is wanted. No committer has yet commented on the approach, and back-branch intent is not stated.

Postgres has no feature, option or extension that keeps these targets across the rebuild. The only workaround is to run alter index ... set statistics or alter statistics ... set statistics again by hand, and that needs the user to know the loss happens, which the current behavior hides. The patches reuse the capture path that already keeps the comment and the owner, so they add no second mechanism. The overlap with Melanie's other series is about which thread carries the patch, and the design is not in dispute.

This is a bug fix: alter column type silently drops statistics targets that users set on purpose, which follows the same pattern as the owner reset already fixed upstream. Its cost falls only on the rebuild path, and asking for field reports before fixing silent loss of user configuration would not be a fair demand objection.
